symmetric pair; this PR brings keras to parity for the non-overlapping
case (strides == size, channels_last).

Scope (intentionally narrow for review):
- Non-overlapping reconstruction only (strides == size).
- channels_last only.
- padding "valid" and "same".
- 2D and 3D variants.
- output_size required (caller must pass it explicitly; for "same"
  padding the original spatial extent cannot be derived from patches
  alone since `(D=25, size=16)` and `(D=32, size=16)` both produce
  `gD=2`).

Out of scope (planned as incremental follow-up PRs):
- overlapping strides + reduction="mean"/"sum" (PyTorch Fold parity for
  the overlap case)
- channels_first
- dilation_rate
- output_size auto-infer for "valid"
- ExtractPatches{2,3}D Layer wrappers
- dual-input dynamic output_size

Implementation:
The non-overlap path is pure reshape -> transpose -> slice. No new ops,
no math beyond layout:

1. Reshape patches (B, gH, gW, pH*pW*C) -> (B, gH, gW, pH, pW, C)
2. Transpose to (B, gH, pH, gW, pW, C)
3. Reshape to (B, gH*pH, gW*pW, C) (the padded canvas that the forward
   conv would have seen)
4. For padding="same": slice off the padding using the same
   `pad_before = total // 2` convention that backend.nn.conv("same")
   uses on the forward pass (verified consistent across TF, JAX, and
   PyTorch backends).
5. For padding="valid": no slicing.

This is the inverse of the conv-with-identity-kernel that
_extract_patches_* uses internally, but implemented without
conv_transpose since stride==kernel makes it tilewise reversible.

API:
  keras.ops.image.reconstruct_patches(
      patches, size, output_size, strides=None, padding="valid",
      data_format=None,
  )
  keras.ops.image.reconstruct_patches_3d(
      patches, size, output_size, strides=None, padding="valid",
      data_format=None,
  )
  keras.layers.ReconstructPatches2D(size, output_size, padding=...)
  keras.layers.ReconstructPatches3D(size, output_size, padding=...)

Naming and argument names match the forward op exactly so the two
compose cleanly.

Tests:
- Roundtrip identity: for a variety of shape combinations (divisible
  and non-divisible), reconstruct(extract(x)) == x to atol=1e-6 across
  TF, JAX, PyTorch backends. The non-divisible cases specifically
  exercise the padding="same" crop path that's easy to get wrong by
  hand (the `pad_before = total // 2` distribution must match what
  backend.nn.conv("same") does on the forward pass).
- Symbolic shape inference: KerasTensor inputs flow through and
  produce correct output shapes (compute_output_spec).
- get_config / from_config round-trip.
- Error paths: invalid size length, invalid padding string, etc.

11 files changed, +851 lines. All tests pass on TF, JAX, and PyTorch.

* Address review feedback on reconstruct_patches PR

- Fix api_gen ordering for keras.ops.image.reconstruct_patches{,_3d}
  (was misplaced between gaussian_blur and hsv_to_rgb).
- Validate output_size is a tuple/list in the public ops (gemini-medium).
- Range-check output_size against grid x patch size for padding='same' in
  both _reconstruct_patches_2d and _reconstruct_patches_3d when the grid
  dim is statically known, so invalid output_size raises ValueError
  instead of silently corrupting the reconstruction (gemini-high).
- Catch data_format='channels_first' early in ReconstructPatches{2,3}D
  __init__ rather than failing later inside call (gemini-medium).
- Add tests for each new error path; clean up unused imports and the
  redundant ternary in ReconstructPatches3D.compute_output_shape.

* Boost patch coverage for reconstruct_patches{,_3d} and layers

- Simplify ReconstructPatches{2,3}D.compute_output_shape: the InputSpec
  + early channels_first check in __init__ guarantee 4D/5D channels_last
  input, so the rank- and data_format-dispatch branches were dead code.
  Both files now at 100% line + branch coverage.
- Add image_test.py tests for the previously uncovered error and edge
  paths in reconstruct_patches / reconstruct_patches_3d: invalid size
  type, invalid size length, invalid output_size length, invalid padding
  string, "valid" padding shape mismatch, "same" padding range checks
  for width / height / depth, non-divisible flat dim, unbatched input
  with int `size`, int `strides`, and the 3D dispatch via the generic
  `reconstruct_patches` op.
- Add `test_int_size` / `test_invalid_output_size` to both layer test
  files so the int->tuple normalization and length check in __init__
  are covered.

* Fix ReconstructPatches{2,3}D tests under channels_first default

The torch CI job runs with image_data_format=channels_first (see
.github/workflows/config/torch/keras.json). The layer test cases
constructed ReconstructPatches{2,3}D without an explicit data_format,
so they inherited the channels_first default and hit the
NotImplementedError guard in __init__ -- failing every test that
builds a layer (roundtrip, get_config, int_size, dynamic_spatial_dim)
while the __init__-validation tests passed. numpy/jax/tf/openvino CI
configs default to channels_last, so only torch was affected.

Pin channels_last in setUp/tearDown for both layer test classes,
mirroring keras/src/ops/image_test.py, so the suite is independent of
the backend's default image_data_format.

* Strengthen reconstruct_patches validation, docs, and op-level tests

- Mirror the eager checks in ReconstructPatches.compute_output_spec
  (flat-dim divisibility, valid-padding grid*size match, same-padding
  range) so invalid graphs fail at build time instead of on the first
  real call. Existing image ops (e.g. RGBToGrayscale) validate
  symbolically the same way.
- Raise NotImplementedError for channels_first in the op class
  __init__ so symbolic use fails as early as eager use.
- Add explicit rank validation to the eager 2D/3D paths, mirroring
  the symbolic error message instead of a raw backend reshape error.
- Correct docstrings: only channels_last is currently supported, and
  output_size for padding='valid' is grid*size (the region covered by
  the patches), not the pre-extraction shape.
- Add op-level tests: extract->reconstruct round-trip correctness
  (2D/3D, valid/same, unbatched, non-divisible crop, int dtype),
  strides/channels_first guards, symbolic validation, wrong ranks,
  and direct Operation-class use.

* Trim PR to ops only: remove ReconstructPatches{2,3}D layers

Per review, keep this PR scoped to the ops, matching how
extract_patches and ops.fold/unfold shipped. The
ReconstructPatches2D/3D layers and their tests are removed; a
Functional model covers the layer use case with the op directly.

The numeric extract->reconstruct round-trip coverage that lived in the
layer tests was ported to ImageOpsCorrectnessTest in a previous commit,
so op-level test coverage is unchanged by the removal.

* Remove reconstruct_patches_3d: reconstruct_patches handles 2D and 3D

Per review, drop the separate reconstruct_patches_3d export.
reconstruct_patches already detects the 2D vs 3D case from the length
of `size` (mirroring extract_patches' internal dispatch), so the
alias only duplicated the API surface. extract_patches_3d exists for
backwards compatibility only and should not gain a counterpart.

- Remove the reconstruct_patches_3d function and its keras_export;
  drop the corresponding entries from the generated API packages.
- Drop the now-unreachable int-size expansion and size-length check
  in the internal 3D helper (the dispatcher guarantees a length-3
  tuple), and reword its error messages to name reconstruct_patches.
- Add a 3D example to the reconstruct_patches docstring.
- Point the tests at reconstruct_patches; the 3D cases now pass an
  explicit length-3 size, since an int size means 2D.

* Fix reconstruct_patches round-trip tests on TPU

The round-trip tests assert reconstruct(extract(x)) == x at atol=1e-6,
which assumes extraction is lossless. extract_patches is conv-based,
and TPUs compute float32 convolutions in bfloat16 by default, so the
extracted patches come back rounded (~2e-3) and the comparison against
the original input fails even though reconstruct_patches itself is
pure reshape/transpose/slice and loses nothing.

Quantize the test inputs to multiples of 1/256 (at most 8 significand
bits, exactly representable in bfloat16), so the identity-kernel conv
is exact in bfloat16 arithmetic and the round-trip stays bit-clean at
the original tolerance on every device.

subject: Reject decompression-bomb members on the .keras asset extraction path (#23101)
message:
Reject decompression-bomb members on the .keras asset extraction path (#23101)

* Reject decompression-bomb archive members on the .keras asset extract path

The decompression-bomb guard `_reject_zip_bomb` is only applied to the
in-memory reads (config.json, model.weights.h5, the shard map). When a
`.keras` archive has more than three members, the loader builds a
disk-backed asset store whose constructor extracts the whole archive
with `ZipFile.extractall`, decompressing every member to disk with no
ratio check. An attacker-added member that decompresses far beyond its
stored size therefore lands on disk in full, exhausting it from a tiny
file under the default safe mode.

Add `_reject_zip_extract_bomb`, which applies the same per-member
declared-vs-stored ratio to every member before extraction. The
per-member ratio is used (not the aggregate) so a bomb member cannot be
diluted by genuine weights stored alongside it; genuine `.keras` members
are stored uncompressed, so the ratio is false-positive-free.

* Address review: trim comments and drop in-test keras import

- Shorten the extract-bomb floor comment to a single line
- Remove the self-explanatory call-site and test-method comments
- Use the module-level keras import in the test instead of a local one

subject: [Bug-Fix] ops.normalize() with order=2 produces NaN gradients for zero vectors (#23093)
message:
[Bug-Fix] ops.normalize() with order=2 produces NaN gradients for zero vectors (#23093)

The L2 (order=2) fast path in `_normalize` computes `rsqrt(square_sum)`
and then clamps the result with `minimum(inv_norm, 1 / epsilon)`. The
clamp fixes the forward value for a zero vector but not the gradient:
`rsqrt(0)` is `inf` and its derivative involves `0 * inf = NaN`, so a
zero vector still backpropagates NaNs. The general `order != 2` path is
already safe because it clamps the denominator before dividing.

Clamp the squared norm before the rsqrt instead, lower-bounding it at
`epsilon ** 2`. Since `rsqrt(epsilon ** 2) == 1 / epsilon` the forward
output is unchanged, while the gradient stays finite for zero vectors.

Adds a regression test that a zero vector has finite gradients on the
tensorflow, jax and torch backends.

Fix keras.ops.roll shift/axis handling to match numpy broadcasting (#23242)

* Fix keras.ops.roll shift/axis handling to match numpy broadcasting

tf.roll, torch.roll and the OpenVINO Roll op all require shift and axis
to have the same length, so valid numpy-style calls such as
roll(x, 1, axis=(0, 1)) crashed on those backends while working on
numpy/jax. Broadcast shift and axis against each other in those
backends before dispatching.

Also validate shift/axis compatibility in Roll.compute_output_spec so
that symbolic inputs raise a ValueError for non-broadcastable
combinations (e.g. shift=[1, 2, 3] with axis=[0, 1]) instead of
silently succeeding while eager execution fails.

* Handle array-like shift/axis in keras.ops.roll broadcasting

isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) missed numpy arrays (and other
array-likes), so shift/axis passed as np.ndarray were wrapped as a
length-1 list instead of being expanded, silently breaking the
broadcasting added in the previous commit and misencoding
Roll.compute_output_spec's validation.

Centralize the shift/axis broadcasting into a single
broadcast_shift_and_axis() helper in backend_utils.py, normalizing via
.tolist() for anything array-like, and reuse it from the tensorflow,
torch and openvino backends plus Roll.compute_output_spec instead of
duplicating the (buggy) inline logic three times.

Also fixes Roll.compute_output_spec crashing when axis is a numpy
array, since canonicalize_axes was called on the raw axis.

message:
Fix Huber, CosineSimilarity and SparseCategoricalCrossentropy losing delta/axis on serialization (#23286)

* Fix Huber, CosineSimilarity and SparseCategoricalCrossentropy dropping hyperparameters in get_config

Huber.get_config and CosineSimilarity.get_config returned only
Loss.get_config(self), dropping delta and axis, and
SparseCategoricalCrossentropy.get_config omitted axis. After a
serialize/deserialize round trip (e.g. saving and reloading a compiled
model), from_config(**config) silently reset these to their defaults:
Huber(delta=2.0) came back with delta=1.0, CosineSimilarity(axis=1)
with axis=-1, and SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(axis=0) with axis=-1,
so a reloaded model evaluated a different loss with no warning.

Store the hyperparameters as attributes and include them in get_config,
matching the pattern already used by CategoricalCrossentropy and
CategoricalFocalCrossentropy. Update test_config assertions and add
serialization round-trip coverage for non-default values.

* Use generic get_config pattern instead of storing hyperparameters manually

Per review, drop the manual self.delta/self.axis attributes and the
hand-rolled get_config overrides in Huber, CosineSimilarity and
SparseCategoricalCrossentropy. LossFunctionWrapper.get_config already
serializes the fn kwargs (delta, axis, from_logits, ignore_class), so
each subclass only needs to pop the non-serializable "fn" entry:

    def get_config(self):
        config = super().get_config()
        config.pop("fn")
        return config

The resulting configs are unchanged, and the existing round-trip tests
still verify that non-default values survive serialization.

subject: Fix GPTQ/AWQ quantization of layers outside the quantization structure (#23321)
message:
Fix GPTQ/AWQ quantization of layers outside the quantization structure (#23321)

* Fix GPTQ/AWQ quantization of layers outside the quantization structure

Model.quantize("gptq"/"awq") used to build quantized variables on every
quantizable layer, while only layers inside the structure's
sequential_blocks were calibrated. Layers outside the structure kept
computing with their float kernel, but saving dropped that kernel (the
gptq/awq serialization spec has no slot for it) and loading marked every
layer calibrated, so reloaded models silently computed with
uninitialized quantized weights.

- Model.quantize now resolves the quantization structure before touching
  any layer (an invalid/missing structure no longer leaves the model
  half-quantized) and only quantizes the Dense/EinsumDense layers inside
  sequential_blocks - the exact set that gets calibrated. All other
  layers keep their original precision.
- Dense/EinsumDense.save_own_variables now raises a clear error when a
  gptq/awq layer is saved without calibration (still reachable via the
  layer-level quantize() API) instead of writing a corrupted file.
- Fixed kernel_zero being silently dropped from every gptq/awq save: the
  LoRA-merged zero point (always None for gptq/awq) shadowed the layer's
  real variable, so saved models failed to load with a variable-count
  mismatch.
- GPTQConfig/AWQConfig.get_config() no longer serialize
  quantization_layer_structure: it holds live layer references, which
  made model.save() recurse infinitely (layer config -> quantization
  config -> structure -> same layer). Like dataset/tokenizer it is
  one-time calibration state.

Adds gptq/awq save/load round-trip tests, guard tests for uncalibrated
saves, a no-mutation-on-missing-structure test, and config
serialization tests.

Stack: phase0 quantization series, PR 1 of 7. Merge PRs in this order,
each rebased on the previous:
  1. phase0/gptq-awq-quantization-scope  <- this PR
  2. phase0/quantize-observability
  3. phase0/serialization-name-keyed
  4. phase0/int4-mode-unification
  5. phase0/quantizer-bug-sweep
  6. phase0/awq-fidelity
  7. phase0/gptq-calibration-perf
This PR is the base of the stack and must merge first. It contains three
commits; the third was folded in from the former
phase0/gptq-serialization-recursion branch, whose remaining content is
regression coverage for this PR's fixes plus a small Embedding hardening.

* Add EinsumDense uncalibrated gptq/awq save guard tests

Mirror the Dense tests: quantizing an EinsumDense with gptq/awq builds
placeholder quantized variables, and saving before calibration must
raise instead of writing a corrupted checkpoint.

* Reject GPTQ/AWQ on Embedding and lock in serialization regression tests

Embedding.quantize now rejects modes other than int8/int4 up front, so an
unsupported calibration mode (gptq/awq) can no longer stash a stale
quantization config on the layer before failing.

Regression tests added for the scoping and serialization fixes in this
PR:
- Mixed Dense + EinsumDense quantized-block save/load round trips for
  GPTQ and AWQ (bit-exact predictions after reload; quantized state and
  config survive the round trip).
- GPTQConfig/AWQConfig serialization drops a *live* layer structure
  (previously caused RecursionError via the layer -> config -> layer
  reference cycle).
- Direct Embedding-level rejection tests for gptq/awq.

Note: folded in from the former phase0/gptq-serialization-recursion
branch, since its remaining content is regression coverage for this PR's
fixes plus a two-line Embedding hardening.

In inject_argument_info_in_error, a failed attempt to set the
_keras_call_info_injected flag on the augmented exception was silently
swallowed, but the augmented (and now unmarked) exception was still
returned and raised. For exception types that reject attribute
assignment after construction, this meant the flag never actually
stuck, so each enclosing Operation.__call__ frame in a nested call
chain treated the exception as not-yet-augmented and wrapped it again,
duplicating the "Exception encountered when calling ..." text once per
nesting level.

Change the except block to return None instead of pass when the flag
assignment fails, so the caller falls back to raising the plain
original exception instead of an unmarked, re-augmentable one.

Added a regression test that raises a custom exception whose
__setattr__ rejects new attributes after construction through two
nested Operation subclasses' call() methods, and asserts the
augmented message text does not appear more than once.

* fix: use self.call's real signature for error-message argument injection

Cond.__call__ and Operation.__call__ passed a local call_fn closure
(generic *args, **kwargs signature) into
inject_argument_info_in_error, so error messages showed generic
args=/kwargs= instead of the real parameter names. Pass self.call
instead so the specific, user-facing signature is always inspected,
including on the symbolic-call dispatch path.

* Clean up house-style deviations and restore lost error context

Style: drop the module docstring, "# ---" section dividers, and
numbered inline comment headers from traceback_utils_test.py (no
other *_test.py file in keras/src/utils or keras/src/ops uses this
decorative structure); restore an Args/Returns docstring on
inject_argument_info_in_error, matching the pre-refactor docstring's
level of detail and current house style (Args:, not the legacy
Arguments:); remove a stale "Wrap self.call..." comment in
Operation.__call__ left over from before this PR's refactor, which no
longer described the code beneath it; and reword the duplicated
"avoids creating a closure" comment in Cond.__call__, where it read as
ambiguous next to the call_fn closure defined a few lines above it.

Robustness: when args/kwargs can't be bound to the callee's real
signature (the arg-count-mismatch edge case noted in review), fall
back to a raw args=/kwargs= dump instead of silently dropping all
argument context. This only runs on the already-slow exception path,
so it adds no overhead to the hot no-exception path this PR exists to
speed up.

Tests: add coverage for the new fallback (bindable-with-fallback and
still-nothing-to-report cases), and add a regression test for the
tf.errors.OpError reconstruction branch, which previously had no
direct test coverage.

* Hoist test-local helper classes to module level in traceback_utils_test.py

_LockedError, InnerLockedLayer, and OuterLockedLayer had real logic
(overridden __setattr__/call/compute_output_spec) but were defined
inline inside a single test method, unlike every other helper class
in this file. Move them to module level for consistency with the
file's own convention and with the rnn_test.py precedent.

* refactor(ops): simplify traceback argument injection per review

- Remove redundant Cond.__call__; inherit error injection from Operation
- Change inject_argument_info_in_error to always return an exception
  with the traceback already set, simplifying callers to a single raise
- Shorten docstrings and remove references to previous implementation
- Remove happy-path test covered by existing layer tests
- Update unbindable-args test to expect original exception returned

* Keep Cond out of rematerialization and harden the raw-argument dump

`Cond.call` receives Python callables rather than tensors, which
rematerialization cannot trace, so `Cond` needs its own `__call__` instead
of inheriting `Operation`'s. Restore it, using the same on-error injection
the rest of this change introduces, and cover it with a `RematScope`
regression test on both scope modes.

`_format_raw_arguments_fallback` joined the result of `tree.map_structure`
directly, but that mirrors the input structure, so a nested argument came
back as a list or dict and the join raised `TypeError`. The surrounding
`except` swallowed it and the whole raw dump disappeared. Render each
result before joining, and extend the fallback test with nested arguments,
which the previous flat-scalar test could not catch.

Also drop the comment above the injection try block in `Operation.__call__`,
which described code that is no longer there, and the test docstring clause
about third-party `call` overrides, which does not affect signature
inspection.

* Drop the PR-context parenthetical from the test class docstring

subject: Fix flaky test_matrix_power: seed the input and condition the negative-power case (#23338)
message:
Fix flaky test_matrix_power: seed the input and condition the negative-power case (#23338)

* Fix flaky test_matrix_power

The negative-power assertion inverts a float32 matrix and compares against
`atol=rtol=1e-6`, but the input was drawn unseeded. The accuracy of a
float32 inverse tracks the condition number of the input, and
`np.random.rand(4, 3, 3) + np.eye(3)` reaches a condition number around 30
routinely and into the hundreds occasionally, which puts the error well
past `1e-6`. The test then fails on unrelated PRs depending on the draw.

Seed the input, following `test_lstsq` in the same file, and raise the
diagonal shift so the matrix is as well conditioned as the
`x_inv_stable` name implies. Condition number drops from ~13 to ~2.1 at
this seed (worst over 300 seeds: ~30.9 to ~2.3), and the largest error
relative to the assertion tolerance becomes 0.04 — a 25x margin — on jax,
tensorflow and torch, and exactly 0 on numpy.

Tolerances are unchanged.

* Trim the comments to what survives the merge

The note on the diagonal shift described the previous `+ np.eye(3)` and
the condition number it produced, which means nothing to a reader of the
merged file. Both comments now state the property the code maintains
rather than the history of the change, and drop to two lines each to sit
closer to the one-line comments used elsewhere in this test.

subject: layers: add TernaryDense — ternary-weight dense layer {-1, 0, +1} (#22960)
message:
layers: add TernaryDense — ternary-weight dense layer {-1, 0, +1} (#22960)

* layers: add TernaryDense — ternary-weight dense layer {-1, 0, +1}

* layers/TernaryDense: fix STE, beta scaling, threshold factor, validation

- Implement Straight-Through Estimator so float kernel stays trainable through
  sign() quantization: kernel + stop_gradient(k_ternary - kernel)
- Apply beta = mean(|kernel|) scaling after matmul when threshold=None,
  per BitNet b1.58 §3.1
- Use 0.5 * mean(|kernel|) as default threshold (was mean(|kernel|))
- Validate threshold is non-negative in __init__
- Update tests: fp-tolerant ternary check, invalid-threshold test, beta test

* layers/TernaryDense: fix ruff lint (unused import, long lines)

* layers/TernaryDense: fix import sort order in API __init__ files

TernaryDense (ternary_dense, t) must sort after reversible_embedding (r)
and before wrapper (w), not after embedding (e).

* fix(ternary_dense): sort TernaryDense import alphabetically in src/layers/__init__.py

* layers/TernaryDense: add ternary quantization for export and inference

Adds a real `quantize("ternary")` path so a trained TernaryDense can be
exported and run inference with the kernel stored at ~1.6 bits/value
instead of float32 with a forward-quantize.

The {-1, 0, +1} kernel is packed five trits per byte (base-243, since
3 ** 5 == 243 <= 256), the log2(3) ~= 1.58-bit information floor. That is
~2.5x denser than int4 and ~5x denser than int8, and lossless. Quantizing
freezes exactly the straight-through forward value, so the layer's outputs
are unchanged; inference unpacks the kernel and applies the BitNet b1.58
scale.

Mirrors the existing int8/int4 quantization machinery:
- quantizers.pack_ternary / unpack_ternary codec
- "ternary" quantization mode + TernaryQuantizationConfig
- quantized_build / _ternary_call and save/load round-trip of the packed
  kernel + scale
- quantize("ternary") packs the trained kernel and sets the dtype policy

Tests cover the codec, quantized-forward equivalence, packed storage at
1.6 bits/weight, and full model save/load round-trip.

* layers/Dense: add quantization_mode="ternary" with sparseskip inference

Dense.quantize("ternary") now packs a trained float kernel to the
information-theoretic floor of ~1.58 bits/value (five trits per byte,
3^5=243<=256, BitNet b1.58 rule: threshold=0.5*mean(|W|)).

Inference uses the sparseskip kernel (_ternary_call): the unpacked trit
matrix is split into two boolean masks (pos=+1, neg=-1). Each matmul
reduces to pure additions with zero weights skipped, eliminating float
multiplies on kernel values entirely.

TernaryDense._ternary_call updated to the same sparseskip pattern.
Docstring updated to clarify the two-path story: TernaryDense for STE
training, Dense.quantize("ternary") for post-training export.

Variable serialization, save/load, dtype policy, and the kernel property
all handle the "ternary" mode.

* tests(ternary): add coverage for Dense.quantize("ternary") and TernaryDense edge paths

- dense_test.py: 7 new tests covering _ternary_build, _ternary_call, the
  kernel property ternary path, quantize("ternary") with/without bias,
  beta scale storage, packed density assertion, and model save/load.
- ternary_dense_test.py: 7 new tests covering subclass type_check guard,
  quantized_build invalid mode, variable_serialization_spec, save/load
  with use_bias=False (no-bias branch in save_own_variables/load_own_variables),
  and dtype_policy post-quantize state.

Addresses codecov gap reported on #22960.

* docs(ternary): clarify quantize('ternary') is storage-only, no inference speedup

_ternary_call unpacks the packed kernel to full float on every forward
pass and runs a standard matmul, so there is no compute or
runtime-memory saving versus a plain Dense layer. Inference is slightly
slower than Dense due to the per-call unpack. The only benefit is
checkpoint size (~1.58 bits/weight, ~5x vs float32, ~2.5x vs int4).

Realizing multiply-free BitNet speedups requires a native ternary matmul
kernel reading the packed format directly; that is out of scope here.

Addresses review feedback from JyotinderSingh.

* fix(ternary): initializer bug, pack_ternary clip, unpack_ternary dtype guard + fast path

- _ternary_build (ternary_dense.py + dense.py): initializer was "zeros"
  (uint8 byte 0), whose five base-3 digits all decode to trit -1, giving
  an all-minus-one kernel before weights load. Fix: Constant(121) — byte
  121 = 1+3+9+27+81, the canonical all-zero-trit byte.

- pack_ternary: clip values to [-1, 1] after rounding before packing.
  round(1.6) = 2, digit 3 overflows base-3 and corrupts the adjacent
  trit on unpack (phantom neighbor). Public API, so clip is safer than
  raising.

- unpack_ternary: add uint8/int8 dtype guard (mirrors unpack_int4 pattern;
  silently running floor_divide/mod on float input returns garbage).
  Add fast path for axis=0 rank=2 (the _ternary_call hot path) that
  skips both transpose ops.

- Docstring: restore accurate sparseskip framing. Design is structurally
  multiply-free (pos/neg boolean mask split). BLAS limitation noted
  honestly; native ternary kernel needed for full compute speedup.

* style: fix E501 line-too-long in ternary_dense.py, dense.py, ternary_dense_test.py

* feat(ternary): add TernaryDTypePolicy stub for future extensibility

Mirrors Int4DTypePolicy / GPTQDTypePolicy / AWQDTypePolicy pattern:
a dedicated class for the ternary quantization mode so per-layer config
(e.g. a custom threshold or kernel spec) has a home when needed. For now
it is a minimal subclass of QuantizedDTypePolicy with no extra state.

_get_quantized_dtype_policy_by_str now returns TernaryDTypePolicy
instead of the base QuantizedDTypePolicy for ternary policies.

* style: fix E501 in dense.py comment shifted by if-statement reformat

* fix(tests): fix ternary Dense test assertions and import order

- Remove incorrect assertAllClose(y_float, y_quantized) from four tests:
  Dense.quantize("ternary") is lossy (float→{-1,0,+1}×β), so outputs
  differ from the float baseline; verify shape equality instead.

- Change assertAlmostEqual(places=5) to delta=1e-5 in beta_scale test:
  Keras TestCase does not support the `places` kwarg.

- Rewrite test_dense_prebuilt_ternary_mode to use dtype="ternary_from_float32"
  instead of the invalid quantization_mode= constructor kwarg.

- Fix alphabetical import order in keras/src/dtype_policies/__init__.py:
  TernaryDTypePolicy must sort after QuantizedFloat8DTypePolicy (T > Q);
  wrong order caused ruff --fix to modify the file and fail the api_gen hook.

- Minor ruff-format fixes in dense.py: expand multi-element tuple in
  `not in (...)` check and reformulate kernel_ternary assignment.

* fix(tests): fix two remaining ternary test failures

- assertAlmostEqual(delta=) not supported by Keras TestCase;
  switch to assertAllClose(atol=1e-5) for beta_scale test.
- Dense._ternary_call() missing **kwargs caused TypeError when
  model.predict() passes training=False; add **kwargs to signature.

subject: Make model.quantize() observable and fail-safe (#23345)
message:
Make model.quantize() observable and fail-safe (#23345)

* Make model.quantize() observable and fail-safe

Problem
-------
`model.quantize()` was opaque and could leave the model in a broken state:

- It emitted one `UserWarning` per non-quantizable leaf layer (a "warning
  storm" on any real model), and silently swallowed every `AttributeError`
  raised during a layer's `quantize()` (`except AttributeError: pass`),
  hiding real bugs behind the "unsupported layer" path.
- It returned `None` and exposed no record of what was quantized, skipped,
  or why.
- Calling `quantize()` on a model that already contained a quantized layer
  died with `ValueError: Layer '...' is already quantized ...`, so a
  partially-quantized model could never be finished with a second pass.
- For structure-aware modes (`gptq`/`awq`), it mutated every `Dense`
  (allocated packed buffers, swapped dtype policies) in the per-layer loop
  and only afterwards resolved/validated `quantization_layer_structure`. A
  missing structure raised `ValueError` after the mutation, leaving the model
  half-quantized.

Change
------
- New module `keras/src/quantizers/report.py` with `QuantizationReport`
  (quantized `[(path, mode, scheme)]`, skipped `[(path, reason)]` with the
  reason distinguishing `no quantize support` / `filtered out` /
  `already quantized`, and an `errors` list).
- `Model.quantize()` now collects a `QuantizationReport` during the loop and:
  * emits ONE summary warning (counts + up to 5 example layer names) instead
    of the per-layer storm;
  * only treats `NotImplementedError` as "unsupported layer" — any other
    exception (e.g. `AttributeError`) now propagates;
  * distinguishes skip reasons via pre-checks (`filters`, `_is_quantized`);
    already-quantized layers are now recorded as `already quantized` skips
    and the rest of the model proceeds, where this previously was a fatal
    `ValueError`;
  * excludes `InputLayer`s from the report entirely — they carry no
    weights, so counting them as "skipped" only added noise to the totals
    and to the warning's example names;
  * gained a `verbose` argument that prints the report;
  * attaches the report to `model._quantization_report` and returns it
    (previously returned `None`). `quantize_wrapper` in `layer.py` was
    updated to propagate the return value.
- GPTQ/AWQ fail-safe: structure resolution/validation is moved BEFORE the
  layer-mutation loop, so a missing/invalid structure leaves the model
  completely untouched (float kernels, original dtype policies, no buffers).
- Public API: the report is exported as `keras.quantizers.QuantizationReport`
  with the skip reasons declared as class attributes
  (`QuantizationReport.SKIP_NO_SUPPORT` / `SKIP_FILTERED` /
  `SKIP_ALREADY_QUANTIZED` / `SKIP_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE`); there are no
  module-level reason constants. Generated API files updated.
- New `Model.quantization_summary()` prints, per quantized layer, the path,
  dtype policy, and weight storage dtype + bytes, plus totals (params,
  quantized bytes vs float32 bytes). The implementation lives in
  `summary_utils.py`, following the `Model.summary()` pattern.

Evidence
--------
`quantization_summary()` on a Dense(256->128) model reports honest storage:
- int8:                 20480 vs 163840 bytes -> 4.00x
- int4 per-channel:     16384 vs 131072 bytes -> 8.00x
- float8:               163840 vs 163840 bytes -> 1.00x (no storage savings)
Mixed functional model (Dense, relu, Dense, 2 InputLayers): quantized=2,
skipped=2 (no support), exactly one summary warning (was 3+ warnings before).
GPTQ without structure: raises before mutation; all Dense keep float32
kernels + original policies, no `quantized_kernel`, no `_quantization_report`.
No benchmark/gist required for this branch.

Test plan
---------
New `keras/src/quantizers/report_test.py` covers the `QuantizationReport`
API (add/query, skip-reason class attributes, single-warning capping at 5
examples, filtered-only => no warning, render sections, repr).
Extended `keras/src/models/model_test.py` with: report contents on a mixed
functional model; filtered skip reason; exactly one summary warning
(`warnings.catch_warnings` count); `verbose=True` prints the report;
`AttributeError` from a broken custom layer propagates; gptq-without-structure
raises AND leaves the model untouched; and `quantization_summary` storage
reporting for int8.

Commands (JAX backend, CPU-only) and results:
  KERAS_BACKEND=jax CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest \
    keras/src/quantizers/report_test.py \
    keras/src/models/model_test.py -k "quantize or quantization" \
    keras/src/quantizers/gptq_test.py -k "scenario" \
    keras/src/quantizers/awq_test.py::AWQIntegrationTest::test_model_quantize_requires_structure \
    keras/src/layers/layer_test.py -k "quantize"

Caveats/Non-goals
-----------------
- `verbose` defaults to `True`; printing routes to stdout only when
  interactive logging is enabled (otherwise to absl logging), so
  non-interactive jobs are not spammed.
- The float baseline in `quantization_summary` is float32; `errors` on the
  report is reserved (empty in the default flow, since real errors propagate).
- Contrary to a prior note, the string mode `"int4"` resolves to grouped
  `block_size=128` through the public `quantize()` API (the wrapper builds a
  default `Int4QuantizationConfig`); per-channel requires an explicit
  `block_size=-1`/`None`.
- Scope: only `Model.quantize`, `quantize_wrapper`, `summary_utils`, and the
  new report module.

Review follow-up (#23345)
-------------------------
- Removed `compute_path_label` entirely (function, export, summary column,
  tests): static hardware/runtime claims do not belong in an API that looks
  authoritative but cannot track backend reality.
- Skip reasons are class attributes on `QuantizationReport` only; the
  module-level constants were removed (the `keras.src` module is private).
- Restored the `_flatten_layers()` leaf check in the quantize walk and the
  summary loop; the `_layers` fast-path was not a valid leaf test (e.g.
  `Dense(10, activation=keras.layers.ReLU())` has sub-layers).
- Dropped `keras.utils.io_utils` mentions from public docstrings (private
  namespace).
- Moved the `quantization_summary` implementation into `summary_utils.py`.

Rebase note: rebased onto the structure-scoping PR. The quantization walk
now also reports gptq/awq layers that fall outside the quantization layer
structure (new SKIP_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE reason) instead of quantizing them;
the early structure resolution this PR originally introduced is already
part of PR 1 of the stack.

Stack: phase0 quantization series, PR 1 of 6 remaining (the original
PR 1, phase0/gptq-awq-quantization-scope, merged upstream as #23321).
Merge the remaining PRs in this order, each rebased on the previous:
  1. phase0/quantize-observability  <- this PR
  2. phase0/serialization-name-keyed
  3. phase0/int4-mode-unification
  4. phase0/quantizer-bug-sweep
  5. phase0/awq-fidelity
  6. phase0/gptq-calibration-perf
This PR is now the base of the remaining stack and must merge first,
before phase0/serialization-name-keyed.

* Quantize layers that own sub-layers; drop the topology-based leaf skip

The quantization walk skipped any layer whose `_flatten_layers()` had
more than one entry. That test conflated "container" with
"unquantizable": a `Dense` with a `Layer` activation (e.g.
`Dense(10, activation=ReLU())`) owns a sub-layer and was silently
skipped. The only thing the topology test actually guarded against was
calling `quantize` on a nested sub-model, which would recurse into a
second full walk; guard exactly that with an isinstance test instead,
and let every other layer decide for itself by raising
`NotImplementedError`.

`find_layers_in_block` in gptq_core had the same topology assumption,
which hid such layers from GPTQ/AWQ calibration (and, combined with
the structure scoping, from gptq/awq quantization entirely); it now
collects every Dense/EinsumDense reachable inside the block.

Fix R2Score num_samples inflation and refactor for readability (#23334)

- Corrected num_samples calculation to count unique active samples across all outputs, avoiding N x K inflation in multi-output regression.
- Simplified implementation using ops.any and ops.sum to ensure an integral sample count.
- Addressed reviewer feedback regarding readability and redundant casts.
- Verified against scikit-learn adjusted R2 baseline.
